_source: Kurnool_Consolidated_Assessment_Report.docx (PIF, August 2026). Figures transcribed as printed; nothing computed here.

levels.label: District training

baseline.topic: Swarna Andhra @2047 vision and foundational GVA/GDP concepts
baseline.strongest: Identifying the name of the Swarna Andhra @2047 vision (100% correct)
baseline.weakest: Which option is not a core pillar of the vision, and the meaning of the bottom-up approach to District Domestic Product (57 to 69% accuracy)
baseline.read: Strong command of the vision and foundational GVA/GDP concepts.

endline.topic: GVA/DDP concepts and district-level economic estimation methodology
endline.strongest: The broad sector covering agriculture, livestock, forestry, fishing and mining (100% correct)
endline.weakest: The key limitation in estimating district domestic product, and constant-price estimation methodology (both around 40% accuracy)
endline.caveat: n=5 for this round; percentages are indicative only.
endline.read: Strong command of GVA/DDP concepts and estimation methodology.

levels.comparison: The baseline (12 questions on the vision and foundational concepts) and the endline (14 questions on GVA/DDP and estimation methodology) tested different, though related, content, so a direct percentage-point comparison would not be meaningful. Read independently, 81.0% at baseline and 80.0% at endline both indicate that officers engaged substantively with the material at each stage.

levels.label: Constituency training

baseline.topic: Sector-wise GVA growth drivers, value addition, outcome indicators and departmental convergence
baseline.read: Moderate-to-strong prior understanding of GVA and convergence concepts.

endline.topic: Same nine questions and answer key, plus a nine-statement training feedback block
endline.read: Moderate-to-strong post-training understanding of GVA and convergence concepts.

levels.comparison: Both waves used the same nine questions and answer key, so the comparison is meaningful. The endline mean is 0.35 marks higher (+3.8 pp); on a Welch two-sample t-test t = 1.46, not significant at the 5% level (p = 0.144). The two waves are independent cross-sections, not a matched panel: the mobile-number field is blank throughout, so respondents cannot be linked. The change reflects both learning and differences in who responded.

levels.label: Master trainer programme

baseline.topic: GVA/GDDP concepts and district-level economic estimation methodology
baseline.strongest: Why the production approach matters for district-level economic analysis (94.9% correct)
baseline.weakest: Why officers should monitor high-frequency proxy indicators rather than rely only on the annual MDP publication, and the effect on GVA when input costs rise faster than output (71 to 75% accuracy)
baseline.read: Strong command of GVA/GDDP concepts and estimation methodology.

endline.topic: GVA/GDDP concepts and district-level economic estimation methodology
endline.strongest: The main administrative message of the presentation (100% correct)
endline.weakest: The effect on GVA when input costs rise faster than output, and how district sector GVA is estimated when direct data is unavailable (76 to 78% accuracy)
endline.read: Strong command of GVA/GDDP concepts and estimation methodology.

levels.comparison: The mean score rose from 85.2% at baseline to 90.8% at endline, a change of +5.6 percentage points, indicating the programme improved participants' command of GVA/GDDP concepts and estimation methodology between the two rounds.

_questions_note: best_q / least_q are the question numbers matching the topics the report names as best and least answered. The reports give no per-question accuracy table, so no percentage is attached to individual questions.
